key_insight: Transformer-based circuit generators trained with quantum-hardware feedback produced compact state-preparation circuits for molecular energy estimation at up to 70 qubits.
engineering_relevance: Hardware-trained circuit generation could reduce two-qubit gate requirements for quantum chemistry workflows relevant to organotin photoresist modeling.
method: Train molecular-descriptor-conditioned generative quantum eigensolver policies first on a noiseless simulator, then on IBM Heron hardware.
Use generated circuits for sample-based quantum diagonalization, with a reward penalty discouraging Hartree–Fock-only sampling.
Transfer policies to organotin hydroxides without retraining, then rank and recover cached measurement counts classically without further QPU calls.
evidence_signal: Across 28 runs at 46–70 qubits, 27 achieved energies within 15 mHa of DMRG references (median error: 4.5 mHa); selected circuits at 56–70 qubits used 34–72× fewer two-qubit gates than device-transpiled LUCJ circuits.
watch_item: The four main training runs required 120 million shots, and classical reference energies informed training; these results do not establish end-to-end quantum advantage.
paper_title: A Hardware-Trained Generative Quantum Eigensolver for Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization of Organotin Hydroxides up to 70 Qubits
